items.title: U.N. Live Updates: Abbas and Netanyahu Offer Dueling Speeches
items.summary: The Palestinian leader, Mahmoud Abbas, is addressing the United Nations General Assembly on video after he was denied a U.S. visa. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel will take the stage weeks before pivotal elections at home.

items.title: Police in Poland Arrest Ukrainian Citizen Over Fatal Stabbing
items.summary: The police arrested a Ukrainian citizen on suspicion of carrying out the knife attack, which came as the two countries are trying to steady relations soured by old antagonisms.

items.title: Saudi Arabia Downs Houthi Missiles Targeting Kingdom, Official Says
items.summary: The Iran-backed militia in Yemen fired six ballistic missiles at cities in Saudi Arabia, a military spokesman said. There was no immediate comment from the Houthis.

items.title: Party Close to King Leads in Morocco’s Election as Young Voters Stay Away
items.summary: Early results in legislative elections showed the lowest voter turnout in nearly two decades. Economic frustrations have grown as Morocco is set to co-host the 2030 soccer World Cup.

items.title: Son of Israeli Ambassador to U.S. Critically Hurt in West Bank Attack, Officials Say
items.summary: Neria Leiter, a reserve soldier, sustained life-threatening injuries after a Palestinian man drove into a military checkpoint in the West Bank, the Israeli military said.

items.title: A Corruption Scandal Is Reshaping Brazil’s Presidential Election
items.summary: Allegations embroiling the Brazilian judge who jailed former President Bolsonaro are reshaping an election that has consequences for Latin America and Washington.

items.title: Europe Warns of Russia’s Hybrid Attacks but Struggles to Counter Them
items.summary: If President Vladimir V. Putin was hoping to get Europeans’ attention, he’s succeeded with a series of close-call incursions. The question now is what they will do about it.

items.title: Beleaguered at Home, a Bellicose Netanyahu Heads to the U.N.
items.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel will take to the world stage while fighting for his political future in a critical national election.

items.title: Nigella Lawson and ‘The Great British Bake Off’ Is a Winning Recipe
items.summary: The British food writer — who brought the world the most creative possible pronunciation of “microwave” — has joined the show. By all accounts, she’s on fire. (In a good way.)

items.title: Inside France’s Push to Stop Migrant Boats to the U.K.
items.summary: Thousands of migrants cross the sea between France and England each year, though numbers have fallen amid increased policing.

items.title: White House Still Bars CNN, MS NOW and Politico Despite Court Ruling
items.summary: A federal court ordered President Trump to reverse his ban on the three news outlets around 1 a.m. Thursday, but none were granted entry later that morning.

items.title: Canada Goose Is Ensnared in Trump’s Tariff War With Canada
items.summary: The United States is a key market for brands that manufacture jackets and parkas in Canada, such as Canada Goose and Moose Knuckles.

items.title: A.I. Safety Concerns Go Global

items.title: In a Race With China, German Robots Are Outnumbered 14 to 1
items.summary: A decade after the sale of Germany’s Kuka, Europe is seeking to shift into a higher gear to unlock the potential in robotics and artificial intelligence.

items.title: Investors Are Betting On Devices That Connect the Brain to Computers

items.title: Bond Markets Are on Edge and Oil Prices Rise

items.title: Abortion Pills, Vaccines and Food Safety: F.D.A. Nominee Heidi Overton Faces Senate Confirmation Hearing
items.summary: Dr. Heidi Overton has called mifepristone “dangerous to women.” As a White House aide, she worked to reduce the number of vaccines recommended for children.

items.title: After a Summer of Disruptions, Here Are the 7 New Rules for Air Travel

items.title: The ‘Monster’ Behind Russia’s Global Effort to Evade Western Sanctions

items.title: Elizabeth Holmes to Transfer to Halfway House in August 2027
items.summary: The founder of the blood-testing start-up Theranos was sentenced to 11 years in prison for fraud and had been serving time at a minimum-security federal prison in Texas.
